domain_setting: A clear multi-sport equipment room, pool, court, field, rink, track, and stadium. Each image should identify one sports object or venue through silhouette and restrained sport-specific context.

ambient_palette.equipment: warm wood, cool slate, coral and amber accents, ivory balls, clear product shadows
ambient_palette.water: pale aqua, pool blue, quiet green, bright safety yellow
ambient_palette.venues: chalk-white lines, grass green, ice blue, warm indoor wood and muted stadium slate
ambient_palette.figures: small natural proportions and varied kit colors, with the equipment or venue as the focal point

recurring_scale_anchors: Canvas 304×192; keep equipment silhouettes whole and use grounding shadows.
No lettering, readable numbers, logos, brands, or club marks.
When two similar terms occur, vary silhouette and setting so each is recognizable at thumbnail size.
Use safe, supervised sports contexts and non-graphic scenes.
For venue terms, show boundaries and distinctive surface markings; for equipment, show the characteristic functional form.

polysemy_resolution_table.ball: General sports ball as a neutral round object with color panels, not only a soccer ball or basketball.
polysemy_resolution_table.baseball bat / bat: Both are sports equipment in this sports chapter. Baseball bat is a narrow cylindrical hitter with baseball cues; bat is the broader blade-shaped wooden cricket-style bat with a red ball. Do not use the bat animal (Lesson 55).
polysemy_resolution_table.racket / tennis racket: Racket in this sports-equipment grouping means a sports implement; tennis racket is the wire-strung frame, while racket is a broader compact paddle-like court implement. Avoid the commotion sense unless the lesson gloss explicitly requires it.
polysemy_resolution_table.net: Generic sports net shown as a taut tennis/badminton net across a court, distinct from soccer goal net.
polysemy_resolution_table.field / pitch: Field is a broad outdoor sports field with generic boundaries; pitch is a marked soccer playing surface, distinct from tar/petroleum residue.
polysemy_resolution_table.court / tennis court: Court means a marked tennis/basketball playing surface, not a courthouse or courtyard.
polysemy_resolution_table.pool: Swimming facility with blue lanes and ladder, distinct from cue-sport pool (Lesson 60) and a puddle.
polysemy_resolution_table.gym / gymnastics: Gym is the indoor sports facility; gymnastics is a judged balance/floor activity using apparatus.
polysemy_resolution_table.float / armband: Float is an inflatable ring or buoyant swim aid; armband is a pair of inflatable arm bands worn on the upper arms.
polysemy_resolution_table.track / running track: Running track is a lane-marked oval athletic facility; track is the broader sports course/surface, not footprints or animal tracks.
polysemy_resolution_table.rink / ice rink: Rink is a general smooth skating surface; ice rink is an explicitly frozen indoor arena.
polysemy_resolution_table.uniform: Matching team clothing with a numbered-free shirt and shorts, not the adjective meaning unchanged.
polysemy_resolution_table.bat / bow / hook / glove: Illustrate the sports context named in the chapter group (bat, archery bow, fishing hook, sports glove), resolving away from unrelated animal/body/household senses.
polysemy_resolution_table.racket: The standalone lesson gloss (ばか騒ぎ, 大騒ぎ) indicates a loud commotion, not another tennis racket; show noisy sports spectators. Tennis racket is the equipment item.
polysemy_resolution_table.armband / float: Armband is a cloth captain/identification band worn on one arm; float is a buoyant swim aid such as a ring or inflatable float.
polysemy_resolution_table.lifejacket / life ring: Lifejacket is a wearable buoyant vest with a collar and front buckles; a life ring is a throwable circle, and a swim float is an inflatable play/support ring.
polysemy_resolution_table.oars / paddle: Oars are a paired set pivoting from a boat; a paddle is held freely and is often single-bladed.
